expectations.name: create-from-scan
expected_behavior: Scans manifests, the entrypoint, examples, CI config, and `assets/` for a logo before writing anything
Asks its gaps in one batched round, and the question turn is in the reply — a single numbered list, not a question per turn
Drafts to the blueprint order — header/logo, overview, features, install, usage, configuration — using the repo's real module path, flag names, and commands
Builds and runs the install and quickstart commands it ships, fixing them until they pass, or names the blocking prerequisite
Wraps prose at the repo's own 100-column `max_line_length`, not a hardcoded 80

expectations.name: no-fabrication
expected_behavior: Invents no install command, version number, registry coordinate, or benchmark figure
Asks for each unknown once; a fact the README needs and still lacks becomes an explicit `<!-- TODO: … -->` marker rather than a plausible guess
Deletes an unsupportable claim outright instead of marking it — a TODO asking someone to source an invented number would preserve the invention
Ships no badge pointing at a host the same README tells the reader does not resolve — a header that contradicts the body three lines down is worse than a bare one
Names the remaining `TODO` markers in the reply so the user knows what is left open

expectations.name: improve-member-readme
expected_behavior: Reports the badges row, the `## License` section, and the `## Contributing` section as findings — the root README and the dedicated files own those
Each finding names the template section it comes from — Badges, Nav, Quickstart, License — so the reader can look the rule up without being told it
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit with a one-line fix each, ends with a one-line verdict, and edits nothing before the user confirms
Applies the approved findings on confirmation, then re-runs Verify and states what changed

expectations.name: gomake-example-injection
expected_behavior: Names the evidence that the project uses gomake — the CI step — in the reply, rather than establishing it from the tool being installed
Asks separately, before creating any `.go` file, naming the files and their functions in one batch — the README approval does not cover writing Go source
Writes runnable `Example…` functions in `_test.go` and runs `go test ./...` until they pass, instead of pasting hand-written snippets
Marks each spot with a `<!-- gmmce:<relpath>/<FuncName> -->` comment above an empty `go` fence and runs `gomake :doc:mce` to fill them
Names each injected key in the reply, taken from the target's `Found <key>` lines — the exit status and the `Writing` line are 0 and present either way
Hand-edits no injected fence; a change to an example goes back through its `Example…` function and a re-run of the target

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Reports what it changed by class and count — badges removed, HTML stripped, heading emoji dropped — without pasting the README back
After fixing, states the file path and what changed, each fact once
Does not paste the rewritten README back into chat
Opens with the payload: no preamble, no narration of the scan, no closing summary restating findings already listed

expectations.name: one-nav-aid-and-module-paths
expected_behavior: Emits at most one navigation aid — a nav line or a `<!-- TOC -->` block, never both
Reads the base path from `go.mod` and `git remote -v`, not from the org name or a sibling repo, so nothing says `github.com/acme/foo`
Ships one nav aid and no second one: no table of contents beside it, and no badge row invented for a project whose remote supplies none
Asserts nothing about the repo being public or private and adds no `GOPRIVATE` or auth step from the host URL alone

expectations.name: no-wide-code-fences
expected_behavior: Keeps every code-fence line within the template's width (≤ ~80 chars, hard cap ~100) so GitHub wraps nothing horizontally
Rewrites the `Example…` function to split the output across lines — one `%q` per line — and re-injects, rather than shipping the wide line
Applies the width rule to the example's source lines too, not only its `// Output:` block: the whole body lands in the fence
Re-runs `go test ./...` after the rewrite so the `// Output:` block still matches

expectations.name: gomake-installed-but-project-does-not-use-it
expected_behavior: Does not treat `:doc:mce` appearing in `gomake --list` as evidence about this project — the target is a built-in and lists everywhere
Finds no gomake config, CI step, or existing marker, and so hand-writes any examples the README needs
Introduces no `<!-- gmmce:… -->` marker into the README and authors no `Example…` function for injection: a contributor without gomake could not regenerate them

expectations.name: unrunnable-command-vs-unpublished-package
expected_behavior: Distinguishes the two failures rather than treating both as unverified
Treats the unpublished module as an ordinary state of a fresh project, not as a failure of the run or a reason to withhold the command
Leaves the quickstart command as written and says in the reply that this environment could not run it — the reader is not warned about the author's sandbox
Warns the reader about the install command with a `> [!NOTE]` naming what has to happen first, since an HTML comment is invisible to them

expectations.name: declined-go-source-gate
expected_behavior: Applies the README-only findings on the first approval, then asks about the Go file on its own
States what the file would be — path, the `Example…` functions in it, and that it joins the test suite and CI — so the user is answering a real question
On the no, writes no `.go` file and leaves the snippet finding reported rather than silently fixing or silently dropping it
Does not write the file and mention it afterwards, and does not re-ask later in the same run
